ev.q: During January–March 2022, four persons and five dogs received a clinical diagnosis of blastomycosis.
Two patients had severe disease and required hospitalization, including one adult patient who died.
Among the four persons with a clinical diagnosis of blastomycosis, all experienced cough, fever, and shortness of breath

public_health_question.v: What were the characteristics and possible environmental source of a neighborhood cluster of human and canine blastomycosis in St. Croix County, Wisconsin?

ev.q: A more comprehensive investigation was launched to characterize potential environmental exposure sources in this community.
Cluster of Blastomycosis Among Neighborhood Residents — St. Croix County, Wisconsin, 2022
In response to this cluster, Wisconsin DHS and DATCP issued alerts to physicians and veterinarians in the surrounding counties
two patients had presumptive laboratory evidence of infection, and two had confirmatory laboratory evidence.
Review of surveillance data identified two human cases reported in the same area within 3 weeks of the canine cases.
Environmental assessments identified a river and unpaved paths running through the neighborhoods under investigation.

equity.level_reason: A small cluster investigation with no social-position dimension reported or discussed.

notes: The cluster is set against background (1–5 county cases a year; none in the neighborhood in the preceding 10 years) without a computed contrast, so comparison is recorded as none. Statewide incidence figures are cited from earlier reports as context. Environmental exposure (soil spores, construction) is a suspected source under ongoing investigation.
